stimulus_db: Medications with an unpleasant taste are generally produced only in tablet, capsule, or soft-gel form. The active ingredient in medication M is a waxy substance that cannot tolerate the heat used to manufacture tablets because it has a low melting point. So, since the company developing M does not have soft-gel manufacturing technology and manufactures all its medications itself, M will most likely be produced in capsule form.
stem_db: The conclusion is most strongly supported by the reasoning in the argument if which one of the following is assumed?

choices_db.A: Medication M can be produced in liquid form.
choices_db.B: Medication M has an unpleasant taste.
choices_db.C: No medication is produced in both capsule and soft-gel form.
choices_db.D: Most medications with a low melting point are produced in soft-gel form.
choices_db.E: Medications in capsule form taste less unpleasant than those in tablet or soft-gel form.

steps.body:
Medications with an unpleasant taste are generally produced only in tablet, capsule, or soft-gel form.
PT → (T or C or SG)

The active ingredient in medication M is a waxy substance that cannot tolerate the heat used to manufacture tablets because it has a low melting point.
~T

The company developing M does not have soft-gel manufacturing technology and manufactures all its medications itself.
~SG

steps.label: Conclusion

C

steps.body:
The argument assumes that medication M has an unpleasant taste.
PT

notes.body: Knowing M can be made as a liquid does not help the conclusion. If anything, it opens a fourth option besides tablet, capsule, and soft-gel. Only the premise about unpleasant-tasting medications limits M to those three forms, and that premise applies only if M tastes unpleasant.

This provides the missing assumption.
PT

This suggests that if a medication is produced in capsule form, then it is not produced in soft-gel form.
C → ~SG
Other medications are not relevant to this argument.

This reverses an inference from the evidence.
C → ~PT
